mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of at least 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 6% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 100,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >100,000 for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and real personal savings (RSAFS) signals increased household investment and liquidity, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 2% for more than six months in a low-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for >6 months AND CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.6%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) accelerates above trend indicates a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to margin compression.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND PAYEMS > trend for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 0.5% for five consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 65% of triggered months.
